title: A Difference Without a Distinction: A Measurement Study of Release Trust Evidence in Package Registries
abstract: arXiv:2606.22593v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: A stolen npm token or account lets an attacker publish a malicious version of a popular package. Such uploads skip the project's CI workflow and can lack its provenance, so since November 2025 an opt-in pnpm policy refuses any release with weaker evidence than an earlier one. Maintainers also publish backports by hand; how often the policy blocks them and which attacks it flags is unknown. We test the policy on the latest versions of 1,997 popular and recently updated npm packages, replay its variants and identity pins on reconstructed stolen-credential incidents, and analyze an npm malware advisory census. We also compare publication evidence across five package registries: npm, PyPI, Maven Central, crates.io, and RubyGems. With pnpm 10.29.3, 1.6% of popular and 7.6% of recently updated installs are blocked, mostly by backports, and one security fix backported by hand, semver 6.3.1, causes 14 of the 16 popular failures. translated_title: 无实质区别的差异：包注册表中发布信任证据的测量研究
translated_abstract: 被盗的npm令牌或账户可使攻击者发布流行包的恶意版本。此类上传会绕过项目的CI工作流，并可能缺少其来源证明，因此自2025年11月起，一项可选启用的pnpm策略会拒绝任何证据弱于先前版本的发布。维护者也会手动发布向后移植版本；该策略阻断这些发布的频率以及它能标记哪些攻击尚属未知。我们在1,997个热门及近期更新的npm包的最新版本上测试该策略，在重构的凭据被盗事件上重放其策略变体和身份锁定，并分析npm恶意软件公告普查。我们还比较了五个包注册表（npm、PyPI、Maven Central、crates.io和RubyGems）的发布证据。使用pnpm 10.29.3时，1.6%的热门安装和7.6%的近期更新安装被阻断，其中主要由向后移植引起，而一个手动向后移植的安全修复semver 6.3.1造成了16个热门失败中的14个。该策略……
tldr: 对包注册表发布信任证据的大规模测量研究表明，pnpm的新证据策略主要误伤手动向后移植的安全修复（semver 6.3.1造成16个热门失败中的14个），并首次对比了npm、PyPI、Maven Central、crates.io和RubyGems五大注册表的发布证据状况。
en_tdlr: A large-scale measurement study of release trust evidence in package registries shows that pnpm's new evidence policy mostly blocks legitimate manually backported security fixes (semver 6.3.1 accounts for 14 of 16 popular failures), and provides the first comparison of publication evidence across five major registries: npm, PyPI, Maven Central, crates.io, and RubyGems.
